subtitle: An open-access non-profit digital initiative founded by Michaela Angela Libut (BSIT-3B), dedicated to advancing inclusive gaming environments, digital hardware equity, and youth technology mentorship.

academicMeta.course: Bachelor of Science in Information Technology
academicMeta.subject: Integrative Programming and Technologies (IPT)

founder.name: Michaela Angela Libut
founder.motto: A small idea can become something bigger when you give it room to grow and surround it with people who believe in each other.
founder.leadQuote: I founded CadaArena to bridge the gap between competitive gaming and community well-being. Too many young players get discouraged by toxic lobbies or locked out by hardware costs. Together, we're changing that narrative.

story.heading: Hi, I'm Michaela Angela Libut.
paragraphs: I am an Information Technology student in BSIT-3B, product designer, and the founder behind CadaArena. For as long as I can remember, gaming and interactive digital technology have been central to my creative journey.

Growing up playing multiplayer games and learning programming, I witnessed how virtual worlds could become incredible incubators for friendship, creative expression, and teamwork. However, I also experienced the darker side of online gaming: pervasive toxicity, hostile lobbies, gatekeeping, and the exclusion of students who cannot afford expensive gaming equipment.

I started CadaArena because I wanted to take initiative rather than simply accept gaming culture as it is. For me, CadaArena is a commitment to build the welcoming, accessible digital space I always wished existed — a place where players of all skill levels, identities, and economic backgrounds are celebrated.
story.pullQuote: A small idea can become something bigger when you give it room to grow and surround it with people who believe in each other.

whyNonProfit.heading: Gaming should belong to people, not just profit margins.
whyNonProfit.intro: When establishing CadaArena, colleagues asked why we didn't turn it into a commercial esports league or a paid subscription club. The answer is grounded in our fundamental non-profit charter:

pillars.title: Community Health Over Monetization
pillars.description: Commercial gaming applications are engineered to maximize daily screen addiction and microtransaction sales. By keeping CadaArena a non-profit initiative, our success is measured purely by player safety, psychological wellness, and meaningful peer relationships.

pillars.title: Democratizing Digital Hardware Access
pillars.description: Many talented young people are locked out of gaming and coding simply because hardware is expensive. By operating as a non-profit, we partner with schools and community labs to offer 100% free sessions, open-source games, and device sharing funded in Philippine Pesos (₱ PHP).

pillars.title: Cultivating Peer Mentorship
pillars.description: We believe senior student developers and experienced gamers have a social responsibility to mentor newcomers. CadaArena creates structured avenues for peer coaching without commercial pressures or paywalls.

prototypingLab.title: The Prototyping Lab & Creative Studio.
prototypingLab.description: From UI wireframes and React components to community tournament brackets and discord bots, everything at CadaArena is planned and built right from Michaela's creative workstation.

values.heading: The core principles that shape every decision.

list.title: Creativity & Expression
list.description: Treating gaming as an art form and a gateway to digital storytelling, creative coding, and collaborative design.

list.title: Radical Inclusivity
list.description: Ensuring that every player — regardless of gender, identity, background, or skill tier — feels safe, respected, and heard.

list.title: Continuous Growth
list.description: Viewing skills not as fixed talents, but as muscle built through patient practice, constructive feedback, and mutual support.

list.title: Accessibility & Equity
list.description: Actively removing economic and physical barriers so every student can participate in modern interactive gaming.

milestones.heading: Still learning. Still building.
milestones.intro: CadaArena is an evolving non-profit project. As Michaela develops her programming and product design skills in BSIT-3B, concrete milestones guide CadaArena's roadmap:

items: Host regular weekly toxicity-free casual gaming socials for students.
Launch free introductory workshops on basic game design and coding.
Publish an open-source guide for running accessible games on low-spec PCs.
Partner with collegiate clubs to promote anti-cyberbullying charters.
Establish chartered CadaArena student gaming chapters across regional schools.
Host an annual regional student game jam focused on social impact themes.
Build a community peripheral library offering borrowed controllers & gear.
Advocate for esports wellness and digital ethics across youth organizations in the Philippines.
